name: Can an open floor plan hurt resale in Los Angeles?

mainEntity.name: Can converting to an open floor plan lower resale value in some Los Angeles homes?
mainEntity.text: Can converting to an open floor plan lower resale value in some Los Angeles homes?

acceptedAnswer.text: Open concept is popular, but it is not automatically the best resale move for every property. In some homes, removing too many walls can eliminate needed privacy, wall space, and storage, especially in family homes or smaller layouts. Buyers may also dislike homes that feel too cavernous, echo-prone, or difficult to furnish. In Los Angeles, the most valuable conversions usually improve flow without destroying function. Before committing, homeowners should consider neighborhood expectations, the size of the home, and whether the new layout still supports dining, living, and work-from-home needs. The safest strategy is to make the plan feel larger and brighter while preserving useful zones and storage.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, if the conversion removes too much storage, creates awkward furniture placement, or makes the home less functional for buyers who prefer defined rooms. A well-designed open layout usually helps, but not every house benefits equally.
